role: AI Platform Engineer Co-Op Intern, Winter 2027
jd:
Our Mission

Rebuild how the world works, to make institutions work better for the people they serve.

About Brain Co.

Brain Co. builds AI-native operating systems for large, regulated institutions. Each system is built for a specific industry, powered by agents that push real workflows forward. Underneath it all is Atlas, our proprietary platform that keeps customers in control, secure by design, and never locked into one model.

Why Now

Brain Co. is entering its next phase of production deployments on a national scale with an elite team built from Palantir, Google, Meta, and Nvidia, and a growing footprint across government, insurance, health, and financial services.

Joining now means shaping both the company and a new category of applied AI. Every project here ships to production and is expected to create measurable customer value and impact.

You'll work alongside exceptional peers on some of the hardest problems in applied AI. It’s the kind of work you'll still be proud of in ten years from now.

About The Co-Op

As an AI Platform Engineer Co-Op Intern, you’ll work alongside experienced platform and infrastructure engineers to help build the systems that power Brain Co.’s AI applications in production.

This internship is designed for current undergraduate students (junior or senior ) who want hands-on experience contributing to real production systems, while receiving mentorship through code reviews, design discussions, and hands-on collaboration with the team. You’ll gain hands-on experience with cloud infrastructure, Kubernetes, distributed systems, observability, and the infrastructure behind modern AI workloads.

What You’ll Work On



- Help build and improve Kubernetes- and Terraform-based infrastructure across production and customer environments.
- Contribute to tooling and automation that makes infrastructure easier and safer for engineers to deploy and operate.
- Work with cloud infrastructure, networking, CI/CD, and containerized systems.
- Help build and improve metrics, logging, tracing, dashboards, and monitoring for production services.
- Investigate performance and reliability issues across distributed systems and AI workloads.
- Support infrastructure for AI inference, data pipelines, and large-scale backend services.
- Participate in code reviews, architecture discussions, and technical problem-solving alongside experienced engineers.
- See the infrastructure you build support real applications used by customers at scale.

You Might Be a Great Fit If You…



- Are a current undergraduate student, specifically a junior or senior, pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Data Science, or a related field
- Have strong software engineering fundamentals and experience programming through coursework, internships, research, or personal projects.
- Have experience with a programming language such as Python, Go, Java, C++, or similar.
- Have exposure to or an interest in cloud infrastructure, distributed systems, operating systems, networking, or databases.
- Are familiar with or excited to learn technologies like Kubernetes, Terraform, Docker, AWS/GCP/Azure, and observability tools.
- Enjoy understanding how systems work under the hood and solving problems involving performance, reliability, and scale.
- Are curious, proactive, and excited to learn quickly in a fast-paced engineering environment.
- Enjoy taking ownership of technical problems while learning from experienced engineers.

What You’ll Gain

Co-Op Details & Benefits



- Winter / Spring Co-Op: January 11, 2027 - April 30, 2027
- Competitive co-op compensation
- Hands-on mentorship from experienced AI engineers and researchers
- Opportunity to work on real production systems used globally
- Potential return-offer consideration for future internships or full-time roles
- Daily lunches (if onsite)
fit_why: Core infra role (K8s/Terraform); candidate's strengths are full-stack and Docker

As a Platform Security Engineer Co-Op Intern, you’ll work alongside experienced security, platform, and infrastructure engineers to help build security directly into how Brain Co. develops and ships software.

This co-op is designed for current undergraduate students, specifically juniors or seniors, who want hands-on experience securing real production systems. You’ll contribute to projects across CI/CD, cloud infrastructure, Kubernetes, containers, and Infrastructure-as-Code while receiving mentorship through code reviews, design discussions, and hands-on collaboration with the team.

This is a builder-focused security role. You’ll learn how security tooling and automated guardrails can make the secure path the easy path for engineers.

What You’ll Work On



- Help build and improve security controls in CI/CD pipelines, including static analysis, secrets scanning, dependency checks, and automated policy enforcement.
- Contribute to developer-facing security tooling, such as linting rules, reusable workflows, automation, and guardrails.
- Help secure Kubernetes and containerized workloads, including access controls, image security, workload configuration, and deployment policies.
- Contribute to security baselines in Terraform and Infrastructure-as-Code, including IAM, networking, encryption, and secure defaults.
- Work with cloud infrastructure across AWS, GCP, or Azure to identify misconfigurations and improve security visibility.
- Help automate the detection and remediation of common security issues.
- Participate in threat modeling, code reviews, and architecture discussions alongside experienced security and platform engineers.
- Work with engineers to understand security findings and turn them into practical, actionable fixes.
- Help improve documentation and tooling so security controls are easy for developers to understand and adopt.

You Might Be a Great Fit If You…



- Are a current undergraduate student, specifically a junior or senior, pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Cybersecurity, or a related technical field.
- Have strong software engineering fundamentals through coursework, internships, research, or personal projects.
- Have experience programming in Python, Go, Java, C++, Bash, or a similar language.
- Have exposure to or a strong interest in application security, platform security, cloud security, or infrastructure security.
- Are familiar with or excited to learn technologies such as Kubernetes, Docker, Terraform, GitHub Actions, and AWS/GCP/Azure.
- Have an interest in how software moves from code to production, including CI/CD, containers, cloud infrastructure, and deployment workflows.
- Enjoy thinking about how systems can fail, where trust boundaries exist, and how security controls can prevent problems without slowing engineers down.
- Are curious, proactive, and excited to learn quickly in a fast-paced engineering environment.
- Enjoy taking ownership of technical problems while learning from experienced engineers.

Bonus Points For



- Coursework, projects, or internship experience involving cloud security, Kubernetes, or Infrastructure-as-Code.
- Familiarity with security tooling such as OPA, Conftest, Kyverno, Trivy, Semgrep, or similar tools.
- Experience with secrets management, IAM, or authentication and authorization systems.
- Interest in software supply chain security, including dependency security, image signing, SBOMs, or secure build pipelines.
- Experience building developer tools or automation.

What You’ll Gain



- Hands-on experience building security tooling for production AI systems.
- Practical exposure to CI/CD security, Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, containers, and Infrastructure-as-Code.
- Experience designing security controls that fit directly into real engineering workflows.
- Direct mentorship from experienced security, platform, and infrastructure engineers.
- Exposure to threat modeling, secure architecture, and software supply chain security.
- Ownership over meaningful engineering projects that can ship into production.

Co-Op Details & Benefits



- Winter / Spring Co-Op: January 11, 2027 – April 30, 2027
- Competitive co-op compensation.
- Hands-on mentorship from experienced security and infrastructure engineers.
- Opportunity to work on real production systems used globally.
- Potential return-offer consideration for future internships or full-time roles.
- Daily lunches if onsite.

Why Intern at Brain Co.



- Help secure AI systems deployed across governments, healthcare, and other critical industries.
- Work on security as an engineering problem, not just a policy or compliance exercise.
- Learn directly from engineers and leaders from Tesla, DeepMind, Databricks, and other top engineering organizations.
- Build practical experience with the security foundations behind modern production AI systems.
- Take ownership early and grow quickly through hands-on engineering.
- Thrive in a culture built on speed, curiosity, and impact.

If you’re a current junior or senior who wants to build security into real systems rather than only study vulnerabilities in isolation, Brain Co. is a place to learn, build, and make an impact.

role: Contract Student Worker – AI Validation and Benchmarking Engineer (40hrs / week Full-Time)
jd:
About Zoox

Zoox is an autonomous ride-hailing company building the world's first purpose-built robotaxi — fully electric, bidirectional, with no steering wheel or driver's seat. Backed by Amazon and founded to make transportation safer, cleaner, and more accessible, Zoox designs its vehicles entirely around the rider. We're currently operating in Las Vegas and San Francisco, with Austin and Miami on the horizon, and testing underway across seven U.S. markets.

About Our Part-Time Student Worker Program

Zoox's part-time student worker program puts you at the center of one of the most ambitious challenges in transportation. You'll contribute to real projects, work alongside engineers and researchers pushing the boundaries of autonomous technology, and gain experience that goes well beyond the classroom. We're looking for students who bring strong academic foundations, curiosity that doesn't stop at coursework, and a drive to be part of something that matters.

Role Overview

This role requires supporting the end-to-end validation pipeline for AI tools: maintaining test datasets, running benchmarks, and measuring agent accuracy across routing decisions, classification labels, and structured output fields.

Responsibilities



- Run and maintain the benchmark pipeline, analyzing results to identify routing errors and regressions across agent variants
- Build and expand ground truth datasets used to evaluate agent outputs against known-correct answers
- Identify and address gaps in benchmark validation and support building a more comprehensive evaluation infrastructure to improve validation prior to release
- Develop new evaluation dimensions such as label accuracy and structured output correctness beyond the existing team classification benchmarks
- Investigate failure modes in agent outputs and work with engineers to surface actionable improvements
- Write scripts and tooling to automate data collection, result parsing, and metric reporting
- Document findings, track benchmark trends over time, and present results to the team

Program Requirements



- Currently enrolled in a B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering or a related field
- Available to commit to a minimum three-month assignment
- Able to commit to a minimum of 20 hours per week
- Able to work on-site at one of our office locations
- Must adhere with Zoox confidentiality requirements, including refraining from using or sharing proprietary company information outside of Zoox, such as in academic research, theses, publications, or presentations

Qualifications



- Familiar with Cursor or Claude
- Familiar with Python
- Familiar with evaluation concepts: precision, recall, F1 score, and confusion matrices
- Comfortable working with structured data (CSV, JSON)
- Experience modifying or writing reproducible analysis scripts

Bonus Qualifications



- Prior exposure to LLM-based systems, prompt engineering, or AI agent evaluation
- Experience with Jira or Slack (e.g. ticketing systems, messaging apps)

Closing

We want to be transparent: this is not an internship. The Part-Time Student Worker Program is designed to complement your academic experience by providing meaningful, ongoing work alongside your studies. Rather than participating in a cohort-based program, you'll join a team directly and contribute to real projects with real impact. While the program does not include structured intern programming or a pathway to full-time employment, it offers valuable opportunities to learn, develop new skills, and gain hands-on experience in a professional environment.

Compensation for this role is $30/hour.

This is a contract position; employment will be through a vendor contracted with Zoox. The hourly rate is as posted, and benefits eligibility is determined by the vendor.

About Zoox

Zoox is developing the first ground-up, fully autonomous vehicle fleet and the supporting ecosystem required to bring this technology to market. Sitting at the intersection of robotics, machine learning, and design, Zoox aims to provide the next generation of mobility-as-a-service in urban environments. We’re looking for top talent that shares our passion and wants to be part of a fast-moving and highly execution-oriented team.

Follow us on LinkedIn

Accommodations

If you need an accommodation to participate in the application or interview process please reach out to [email protected] or your assigned recruiter.

A Final Note:

You do not need to match every listed expectation to apply for this position. Here at Zoox, we know that diverse perspectives foster the innovation we need to be successful, and we are committed to building a team that encompasses a variety of backgrounds, experiences, and skills.

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.
fit_why: Benchmark/eval ML tooling; candidate has Python and stats, but no ML eval experience
